The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, March 14, 1924.

SIR, - Referring to your letter of the 13th ultimo, regarding cheque No. 51 for $400 issued on April 23rd, 1923, against
our Manitoba and North West Vote in favour of Mr. R.E. Osborn, In Trust, as an advance for repairs to the Crooked
Lake Agency house, I beg to quote the following explanation furnished by Mr. Osborn in regard to the last paragraph
of your letter, viz.: -

"On April 23rd, 1923, an accountable advance cheque for $300 was received from Commissioner Graham to, apply on
the Woodward contract and on the 24th April the payment of $130 referred to in your letter was paid Mr. Woodward
from this $300.

"Accountable cheque No. 51 for $400 from the Department was received on the 28th April and on the same day a
cheque for $300 was sent to Commissioner Graham to refund the amount received from him on the 23rd thus making
the $130 chargeable to cheque No. 51.

"It will be seen from this that no Trust funds were used to pay Mr Woodward."

With regard to the agreement entered into, with Mr. J. Woodward, I beg to state that a copy was sent to your office by
the Department on the 6th November last, but I herewith enclose another copy.


Your obedient servant,
J.D. McLEAN, Asst. Deputy.

The Assistant Auditor General.

<!-- page 554 -->
AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, March 17, 1924.

SIR, - I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter of the 14th inst., (file No. 21-108), replying to mine of
February 13th with regard to cheque No. 51 for $400 issued on April 23rd, 1923, in favour of Mr. R.E. Osborn as an
advance for repairs to the Crooked Lake Agency house.

In your reply you quote Mr. Osborn as stating that on April 23rd, 1923, he received an advance cheque of $300 from
Commissioner Graham at Regina to apply on the Woodward contract and that on April 28th, when, he received the
$400 advance from Ottawa, he refunded the advance of $300 made by Mr. Graham.

I should like to be informed as to what funds held by Mr. Graham this advance was made from. To the best of my
knowledge the only funds held by Mr. Graham are contained in four Trust Accounts, viz.: - Greater Production
Account, Warehouse Account, Grazing Leases Account, and Indian Bands Trust Account, and from no, one of these
Trust Accounts could the advance have been made without, temporarily diverting moneys held for special purposes.


I am, Sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, March 19, 1924.

SIR, - Reply to your letter of the 17th instant, regarding the advance of $300 made by Commissioner Graham at
Regina, to Mr. R.E. Osborn, Indian Agent, at Crooked Lake Agency, I beg to say that this advance was made from
Mr. Graham's Indian Bands Trust. Fund Account.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
J.D. McLEAN, Asst. Deputy and Sec'y.


The Assistant Auditor General.


Vote 275, Indians of Manitoba, etc.: Employment of Clerk at Lesser Slave Lake Agency without due authority

AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, November 5, 1924.

SIR, - I find from the accounts in support of your expenditure for the fiscal year 1923 - 24 that Mr. B. Wray was
employed by Indian Agent Harold Laird, as clerk at the Lesser Slave Lake agency from July 6 to September 25 and
from October 9 to December 31, 1923, and was paid by Mr. Laird at the rate of $100 a month.

I have no certificate from the Civil Service Commission authorizing the employment of this man. Kindly inform me if
the employment was authorized by the Commission and if not, what authority there was for his employment for a long
period than one month.


I am, Sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

<!-- page 555 -->
The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

<!-- page 556 -->
DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, November 7, 1924.

SIR, - In reply to your letter of the 5th instant, respecting the employment of Mr. B. Wray as clerks at the Lesser Slave
Lake Agency from July 6 to September 25 and from October 9 to December 31, 1923, I beg to say that a clerk's
services were necessary during the annuity payments, but the Indian Agent should have notified the Department
beforehand, so that the appointment could be made in the regular way through the Civil Service Commission. This he
failed to do and employed Mr. Wray without reference to the Department. He is being informed that in future this
appointment will be made through the Civil Service Commission and that he will be notified whom to employ.


Your obedient servant,
J.D. MCLEAN, Sec.


The Assistant Auditor General.

Vote 276, Indians of British Columbia: Adjustments of Previous Payments to Columbia Coast Mission for
Hospital Care, etc.


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, August 22, 1924.

SIR, - British Columbia cheque No. 1579 of 1923 - 24 is for the payment of $797.15 to the Columbia Coast Mission,
Inc., for unpaid Indian Accounts incurred prior to January 1, 1923. This amount is made up as follows: -

Accounts of 1918 - 19       70.00
Accounts of 1919 - 20       267.75
Accounts of 1920 - 21       324.55
Accounts of 1921 - 22      172.75
Accounts of 1922 - 23      70.10
...                        $905.15
Less for 183 hospital days 183.00
...                        $722.15
Doctor's services          75.00
Total                      $797.15

I find that during the period covered by this account the following payments were made by you to the Columbia Coast
Mission: -

Year      Grant for Doctor Treatment
1918 - 19 $600.00          $436.00
1919 - 20 600.00           483.25
1920 - 21 724.99           729.00
1921 - 22 850.00           327.00
1922 - 23 850.00           403.00

In view of the fact that payments were made each year, both for medical services and for hospital treatment, I have to
ask for an explanation of the payment in question. As this institution was in receipt of an annual allowance for medical
